# Suttantikadukamātikā (Ds 1.3)

**ID:** Ds 1.3
**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Suttantikadukamātikā
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ds1.3
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh01m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suttantikadukamātikā* ("List of Suttantika Dyads" or "the dyad matrix from the sūtras") is the third and concluding section of the opening matrix (*mātikā*) of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [U Kyaw Khine 1999; Buswell & Lopez 2014; Tan Poh Beng 2015]. It follows the Abhidhamma triads (*tika*) and Abhidhamma dyads (*duka*), marking the end of the collective *mātikā* before the commencement of the *Cittuppādakaṇḍa* [U Kyaw Khine 1999; Buswell & Lopez 2014].

This matrix classifies doctrinal factors drawn from the Sutta Piṭaka into pairs, enumerated either as 42 or 46 categories of dyads [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Tan Poh Beng 2015]. According to the *Atthasālinī*, the commentary to the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the matrix of suttanta dyads was introduced by the Venerable Sāriputta to facilitate the study and understanding of the Sutta Piṭaka [Buswell & Lopez 2014; Tan Poh Beng 2015]. Nevertheless, modern scholars observe that these dyads remain ancillary to the core Abhidhamma system, as they are not systematically elaborated in the *cittuppāda* or *rūpa* divisions of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, nor are they employed across the other treatises of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Tan Poh Beng 2015].

SuttaCentral notes two modern translations in two languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 109 matching passages with eight other texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments occur with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, the *Suttantikadukanikkhepa* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* itself (Ds 2.3.3, which directly unpacks these dyads), the *Saṅgīti Sutta* of the Dīgha Nikāya (DN 33), the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17), and the *Dukanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 2), along with commentary parallels in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā* and *Pāthikavaggaṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also computes cross-language alignments with Sanskrit works such as the *Dharmasaṃgraha* and the Patna Dharmapada [DharmaNexus].
